title: Add binding inheritance guard and geo-key provenance header
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a guard to prevent cross-geozone inheritance of operator bindings, add X-KMS-Origin-Chain for provenance verification, and consolidate audit events to remove duplication across proxies. Backwards-compatible rollout with shadowing and gradual enforcement.
description: Summary: This PR adds a binding inheritance guard to RBACv2, introduces a lightweight KMS provenance header (X-KMS-Origin-Chain) surfaced through the gateway, and a small audit consolidator used by the audit-forwarder to deduplicate events coming from chained proxies. Motivation: We observed two related classes of compliance gaps in multi-zone customers: (1) operator/service bindings that unintentionally inherited privileges when tenant objects were copied across geozone boundaries and (2) duplicated/misaligned audit entries from edge proxies that obscured key provenance. The changes here are intended to close those gaps with minimal disruption and a staged rollout. What changed (high level): - rbac/policy-compiler: add BindingInheritanceGuard module. The guard enforces that operator/service role bindings cannot be transitively inherited across geozone boundaries unless an explicit 'inherit: true' attribute exists on the target namespace and the tenancy claim includes an allowlist. - gateway/proxy: attach X-KMS-Origin-Chain header (comma-separated list of key-region:provider entries) to internal KMS calls and to outgoing audit envelopes when present. The header is signed by the gateway's operator key when crossing zone boundaries. - audit/forwarder: introduce AuditConsolidator which deduplicates events using (trace_id, request_id, key_provenance_hash) and tags consolidated events with provenance-summary for downstream retention/policy. - admission controller: validate new binding attributes on create/update and reject suspicious cross-zone binds in enforced mode. - policy migration: tooling to scan and annotate namespaces with 'inherit' flags and produce a remediation report. - tests: unit and integration tests for guard, header propagation tests under fault injection, and end-to-end audit consolidation test harness. Rollout plan: 1) Shadow mode (default): BindingInheritanceGuard runs in 'observe' mode, emitting structured telemetry to SLO/alerts and adding findings to the policy-migration report. 2) Canary enforcement: enable enforcement in a small set of non-production tenants for 72h. 3) Gradual opt-in: expose a tenant opt-in flag and run a migration job to annotate safe namespaces. 4) Full enforcement: after 4 weeks of canaries and zero high-severity findings, flip default to 'reject' for newly created cross-zone binding attempts. Backwards compatibility: X-KMS-Origin-Chain is optional. Old gateways without the header continue to operate; the consolidator treats missing provenance as 'unknown' and only applies dedupe heuristics with reduced confidence. Security review notes: The header is canonicalized and signed to avoid tampering; gateway signs using operator's zone key. Audit envelopes containing provenance are stored with a provenance hash to simplify forensic queries. Related work: references ENG-2247 (rbac policy hygiene) and ENG-4902 (kms provenance telemetry). See also SUP-78 (support ticket documenting customer incident). Migration steps included in the PR ensure we do not inadvertently block legitimate operator workflows. The description below includes the checklist and a short runbook for rollback. Checklist: - [x] Policy compiler change unit tests - [x] Gateway header propagation integration tests - [x] Audit consolidate integration tests - [x] Admission controller rejection tests - [x] Migration scanning tool and dry-run report - [x] Documentation updates (RBACv2 policy guide + operational runbook) Runbook (quick): - To disable enforcement quickly set ENV RBAC_BINDING_GUARD_MODE=observe on policy-compiler service and feature flag redwood.rbac.binding_guard=false in config-service. - To remove header propagation set GATEWAY_DISABLE_KMS_PROVENANCE=true and restart canaries. - To revert audit consolidation, flip AUDIT_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=false and reprocess queued envelopes.
commits: 3c47a2d: add BindingInheritanceGuard and associated unit tests
a9b4f7e: emit X-KMS-Origin-Chain in gateway when key provenance known
ff2b1c1: audit consolidator + integration tests + migration scanner
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can you clarify the canonicalization algorithm for X-KMS-Origin-Chain? I want to ensure signing is deterministic across gateways.

Author (Maya Chen): We canonicalize entries as region:provider:keyid sorted lexicographically, then join by comma. The signature is over the canonical string plus request_id. Added comments and unit tests (see gateway/kms/provenance_test.go).
Priya Natarajan: Admissions rejection path looks strict — do we have an escape hatch for operator teams during migration?

Author (Maya Chen): Yes. The admission controller respects RBAC_BINDING_GUARD_MODE env which defaults to observe. We've added a tenant opt-in flag and a CLI remediation tool to annotate namespaces; noted in the docs.
Samir Patel: Audit consolidator dedupe key uses a combined hash; we should include a TTL window in the consolidator to avoid long-term collisions.
reviewer_responses: Maya Chen: Added TTL window 10m in consolidator and made it configurable via AUDIT_CONSOLIDATOR_TTL. Updated tests to cover timing edge cases.
Diego Alvarez: Approved after provenance canonicalization and signature tests were added.
Priya Natarajan: Approved with comment to monitor canary metrics for 72h.
Samir Patel: Left a minor comments fix which was addressed (naming and log level).
merge_result: squash and merge by Diego Alvarez. Commit message updated to include migration notes and release guidance.
notes_for_changelog: Security: Prevent cross-geozone binding inheritance by default and add KMS provenance header to improve key region accountability. Also reduce noisy duplicate audit events with consolidation logic. See docs/rbacv2/geo-inheritance.md for operator guidance.
post_merge_actions:
- Kick off migration dry-run job (tools/migration/annotate_namespaces.py --dry-run) for all tenants in staging.
- Monitor redwood.rbac.binding_guard findings stream for 72h.
- Check audit-forwarder metrics: consolidated_events_rate and dedupe_confidence.
- Add canary tenants to rollout dashboard and watch support ticket SUP-78 for related regressions.
hotfix_followup: If a high-severity failure is observed, set RBAC_BINDING_GUARD_MODE=observe and disable feature flag; run revert step to re-enable previous policy-compiler binary. Audit consolidator can be disabled independently without data loss.
